T: Pines, black with smoke from a hundred campfires.
A: A family's tent, patched with regiment scarves. Inside, someone is practising a war cry, quietly, so as not to wake the baby.
x: A campfire. A pot of something grey. It might be Kaldorbread soup. It might be glue.
n: A tithe banner: the fist crushing a crown, and under it, chalked: ONE FIGHTER OR ONE IRON. PER HOUSE. PER YEAR.
j: A cairn of small stones, one for each fighter who walked this road and didn't walk back.
S: A signpost. NORTH: KALDOR. SOUTH: NOT KALDOR (YET).
^: The road north, back up to the kingdom's south gate.
_: The road south, toward an old watchtower on the hill.

objects.name: Marta
lines: Knitting armour for my boy. He goes to the city in the spring, for the tithe.
Wool armour. I know. But it's very thick wool, and I've put a lot of love in it, and love is heavier than you'd think.

answer: Every house gives one fighter to the pit a year. Or iron, if you've got iron.
Nobody's got iron. The king has all the iron. So it's fighters.
He's a poet. He writes about clouds.
He's going to headbutt somebody, very sadly, and then he's going to write about it.

objects.name: Old Dobb
lines: I've brought my iron. For the tithe.
…It's a spoon. It's iron, though. Mostly. The handle's iron.
If the king wants a fighter out of my house he can have the goat. The goat's meaner than all of us.

objects.name: Sergeant Bellow
lines: (whispering) Tithe camp. Fighters on the left. Iron on the right.
(whispering) Spoons are not iron. Tell Dobb. He won't hear it from me.
(whispering) I can't shout. Never could. The whole squad has to lean in. We're very close as a squad.

answer: (whispering) Born like it. My mum says I came out, looked around, and said 'oh no' very quietly.
(whispering) The horde made me a sergeant to toughen me up. Now everybody whispers back. It's quite nice.

lines: TITHE CAMP. NO FIGHTING IN THE CAMP.
Underneath, smaller: (ALL FIGHTING TO BE SAVED FOR THE PIT.)
